detail: Page 1 expects 'Venture 2022 Snowboard' 8th and 'Venture 2.0 40L Waterproof Duffel Bag' 9th. Under a linguistic collation such as Postgres en_US.utf8, which mostly ignores spaces and punctuation, 'venture2040l...' sorts after 'venture2022...', so name-desc puts the Duffel Bag first. That contradicts the plan's open question, which says name cases assert only collation-stable positions. Assert positions 1-7 exactly and the last two as the set {Venture 2022 Snowboard, Venture 2.0 40L Waterproof Duffel Bag}, or name the collation the stack uses and assert that order.

Page 0 data[*].id is asserted exactly as [30, 46, 1, 55, 11, 9, 33, 22, 67]; whether 22 (Venture 2022 Snowboard) comes before 67 (Venture 2.0 40L Waterproof Duffel Bag) depends on the database collation, the same issue as TC-03. Assert the first seven ids exactly and {22, 67} as a set in the last two places, or name the collation the fixture uses.

The project context requires every e2e case to name the page and the seeded user. TC-BUG-40-01 to TC-BUG-40-10 name the page (`/`) but never say the catalog is browsed anonymously with no signed-in user. Add 'anonymous (no seeded user signed in)' to each e2e case's preconditions, or say it once in _index.md.

It is implemented as a Playwright request test against the test stack in the e2e spec. The assertions are complete, but no functional test exists in the required project, which is present and reachable.

The case expects page 2 of type=3 price-desc to start with Blizzard Rider Snowboard $299.99. The plan's own TC-BUG-40-15 (type=3 page 1 price-desc ids [53, 5, ...]) and the recorded run put Raven Swift Snowboard $349.00 (item 53) first. The test asserts the real order (Raven Swift first, Blizzard Rider second). The case's expected first card must be corrected.

Inconsistent BASE_URL handling (lesson L1): openCatalog calls page.goto('/') through the config baseURL, while TC-BUG-40-09 in the same spec and the neighbouring cat-1.spec.ts and browse-catalog.spec.ts call page.goto(BASE_URL). Use one convention.

Expected bullet 1 says the order applies 'with the active brand and type filters', but brand (TC-05/15) and type (TC-06/15) are only tested on their own. Add a request or UI flow with both active (for example brand=2&type=3&sort=price-asc) asserting the exact ids in order and the count, and the order across pages if the result spans more than one.

The project context requires e2e cases to name the seeded user; TC-01 to TC-10 don't. State that the catalog is browsed by an anonymous (not signed-in) visitor in each e2e case's Preconditions or in the plan index.

The comment before the page-2 assertions says 'The case names Blizzard Rider Snowboard $299.99 as the first card' and justifies 'asserting the real order'. The case actually expects Raven Swift Snowboard $349.00 first and Blizzard Rider second, which is exactly what the test asserts. The misleading comment should be removed so the test does not look like it departs from the spec.
